tasks.short: Provide input into design and manufacturing of new equipment

steps.what: Evaluate new equipment against installation and repair experience
Discuss design and manufacturing improvements with equipment engineers

tasks.design: Retain hands-on evaluation and discussion with the equipment engineer. Existing drawings in {DOCS} support the conversation; generating another summary does not replace the technician's practical contribution.
tasks.previous_blocker: Practical installation and maintenance experience is situational.
tasks.enabler_now: No supported change removes a material part of this contribution.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing manufacturability, repair access and real operating constraints.
tasks.human_edge: The technician notices practical problems absent from drawings.
tasks.altitude: No time or decision-right change; the engineer retains design authority.

reach.learn: Explain field failure modes to designers

evidence.claim: Field-service record capabilities do not establish automation of practical equipment design advice; this retained-work scenario is model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary covers technician evaluation and advice, excluding engineering design, manufacturing and separate service-record entry.

Technician produces practical concerns through s1 observation and experience; its55 hours include identifying and explaining relevant facts. Engineers supply existing concepts through unchanged design work; unclear details are discussed manually.
No new tool or record is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero. Existing document access earns no new saving.
research_questions: Does any substantial repeated preparation exist beyond the practical evaluation and discussion?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100, no incremental upkeep. Practical evaluation and collaborative advice are unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Address unauthorized use and electrical or acoustic shock situations

steps.what: Assess special issues including unauthorized equipment use or shock
Apply authorised immediate safety or equipment protection measures
Escalate unresolved safety or unauthorized use concerns to responsible personnel

tasks.design: Keep situational assessment, authorised physical measures and escalation through {TELEPHONY} human. Existing procedures in {DOCS} guide the response; the design adds no automated judgement about illegality or shock safety.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rare situations differ in immediate hazards and authority requirements.
tasks.enabler_now: No supported automation changes the physical response or accountable judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Uncertain fault conditions and potentially injured people require immediate contextual decisions.
tasks.human_edge: The technician recognises limits of competence and escalates promptly.
tasks.altitude: Existing safety and security decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Safe isolation and incident escalation boundaries

evidence.claim: Physical hazard assessment and incident escalation remain human work in this scenario.

assumptions: Boundary covers technician response, excluding medical treatment, formal legal decisions and separate incident-record tasks.
Technician identifies observed symptoms, affected equipment and location in s1; capture and clarification are included in30 hours. Unknown causes remain unknown and trigger manual escalation.
Existing procedures and communications remain in place, with no new upkeep. No structured incident code is assumed.
research_questions: Are technicians clear about immediate measures and mandatory escalation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 and zero upkeep. The proposal leaves assessment, physical measures and live escalation unchanged.

tasks.short: Place intercept circuits on vacant line terminals

steps.what: Identify vacant lines and verify the intended terminals and circuit arrangement
Place and connect intercept circuits on the verified terminals
Test intercept operation and correct connection faults

tasks.design: Keep terminal identification, physical circuit placement and functional testing manual. Existing instructions in {DOCS} support the work; no remote switching interface or automatic vacancy detection is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical terminals and actual line conditions must be verified locally.
tasks.enabler_now: The digest's record tools do not replace wiring or functional tests.
tasks.still_hard: Mismatched markings or legacy installation changes.
tasks.human_edge: The technician validates actual connections and diagnoses failed tests.
tasks.altitude: No change in hands-on work or service authority.

reach.learn: Terminal tracing and functional test methods

evidence.claim: Circuit placement and local functional verification are retained physical work in this scenario.

assumptions: Boundary covers one circuit installation and testing, excluding separate work-order entry and network design.
Technician verifies line vacancy, terminal identity and intended circuit arrangement in s1, counting all verification time in20 hours. Unclear markings require manual tracing before connection.
Existing test equipment and instructions are baseline tools. No new technology or upkeep is introduced, justifying zero incremental work.
unknowns: Installed terminal technology and verification procedure
research_questions: What proportion of effort is physical connection and test versus separate record entry?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 and zero upkeep. No saving is assigned to physical placement, verification or existing instructions.
